subject: Capacity signalboard: OKR check-in & GPU economics thermostat
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity signalboard: OKR check-in & GPU economics thermostat

Team —

Ahead of Leadership sync next week I want a short, shareable snapshot that ties our OKR progress (Capacity and Unit-Economics) to operational asks. Key asks:

- Current committed GPU slots vs. forecasted demand for the next 90 days (by model class).
- Month-to-date utilization and tail-latency incidents (p50/p95/p99).
- Immediate cost levers we can flip: batching thresholds, prefix/KV caching adoption, quantization candidates.
- Any material runway risk that requires an executive decision (e.g., priority slot reallocation, temporary burst purchase).

Deliverable: a 1-page "signalboard" + 3-slide backup with the numbers and a short recommended action list. If we can have a draft by Friday AM that gives leadership time to react, that would be ideal.

I attached the stress test plan we ran last week — Markus, please attach the result summary and a quick note on what changed from the previous test. Irene/Karthik please call out any actionable playbook items (batching/cache) that would materially alter unit economics.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Attachments: stress_test_plan_q3.pdf (plan stub)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity signalboard: OKR check-in & GPU economics thermostat

Lauren —

Thanks. Quick summary of the stress test results (attached as PDF):

- Committed slots: 480 A100-equivalent slots (after recent scaling).
- Observed peak demand in test: 720 slots sustained for 45 minutes (burst traffic simulation).
- Average utilization (last 30d): 62% at cluster level; p95 utilization 89%.
- Tail latency: p99 token latency increased when effective batch size > 28 for long-form (>1024 tokens) workloads.
- Cost delta: burst to 720 slots increases expected daily GPU spend by ~34% vs baseline.

Actionable notes:
1) Short term: enable prefix KV caching for the two largest LLMs in prod (reduces per-token compute by ~12% in our runs).
2) Mid term: aggressively lower batching threshold for long-form routes during peak windows (trades slight latency for ~18% token cost reduction).
3) If leadership approves, reserve an additional 120 burst slots for the next 60 days to avoid degradation during large customer experiments.

I attached: stress_test_report_q3.pdf (summary), slot_allocation_model.csv (numbers). I can convert the CSV into the one-pager signalboard.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Infrastructure Economics
markus.klein@redwood.com

Attachments: stress_test_report_q3.pdf, slot_allocation_model.csv

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity signalboard: OKR check-in & GPU economics thermostat

Lauren / Markus —

Couple of notes from the runtime experiments and playbook side:

- Batching: Our live A/B test reducing max batch size from 64 -> 32 on the "docs-collate" route cut token compute 14% with a 3–7% median latency increase; p99 was unchanged. We should treat this as low-friction, high-impact for that route.
- KV caching: Prefix caching rollout is at 45% on internal traffic; enabling for customer-facing routes needs a brief compatibility check (function-calls + dynamic prompts). If we greenlight, engineering estimates 2 engineer-weeks to complete and monitor.
- Quantization: We have one strong candidate model (tied to a single enterprise route) that can move to 4-bit experimental quant and yield ~22% GPU cost savings for that route, but accuracy needs to be validated against our evals.

Suggested playbook items for the signalboard:
- Short term (1–2 weeks): apply reduced batching thresholds on identified routes; flip KV caching for internal-only routes to test stability.
- Medium (2–8 weeks): staged KV caching rollout + quantization eval pipeline for candidate model.

I attached the playbook workbook (batching_cache_playbook.xlsx) with route-level recommendations and risk notes.

Irene
Irene Choi
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
irene.choi@redwood.com

Attachments: batching_cache_playbook.xlsx

Thanks everyone — solid inputs.

Plan of record for the Leadership packet (final due Monday AM):
1) One-page signalboard (Markus): top-line committed vs. forecast slots, utilization, and the single-row runway risk decision (reserve +120 slots for 60 days). Include the cost delta and proposed funding source (runway buffer).
2) Playbook slide (Irene + Karthik): short-term route-level changes (reduced batching thresholds, KV caching targets) with estimated % cost impact and risk column. Mark the specific customer-mapped routes so we can call out where credits / SLA work may be necessary (Molly — we'll flag Acme routes explicitly).
3) Exec ask slide: a single decision ask (approve temporary 120-slot burst) + fallback (prioritize slot allocation by enterprise revenue if deny).

Markus — please send the one-pager and the model CSV by Sunday EOD. Irene/Karthik — finalize the playbook workbook with the customer mapping. Molly — appreciate the heads-up; we'll call out your contract routes and proposed mitigations (credits or traffic shaping) in the deck.

I'll assemble the slides and send the draft packet by Sunday midnight for review.

—Lauren
